traceability.evidence: Story file docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md clearly defines requirements REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE, REQ-SUPPORTS-VALIDATE, REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-SUPPORTS, REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT, REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT, REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT, REQ-SCOPED-IDS, REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION and acceptance criteria for @supports behavior.,Rule-level parsing and format validation of @supports is implemented in src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts and its helpers src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-format-validators.ts: processCommentLine() detects '@supports' with /@supports\b/, extracts the value, and calls validateImplementsAnnotation(context, comment, implementsValue, options). validateImplementsAnnotation() delegates to validateImplementsAnnotationHelper with MIN_IMPLEMENTS_TOKENS and reporters for missing value, invalid story path, and invalid requirement IDs. Messages.meta includes invalidImplementsFormat specifically for @supports. This matches REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE and REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION.,Unit tests for @supports parsing and format validation are in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts, tagged for docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md with @req REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE, REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION, REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT. Valid cases include: - "[REQ-IMPLEMENTS-PARSE] valid single @supports with one story and one requirement (default patterns)" - "[REQ-IMPLEMENTS-PARSE] valid multiple @supports lines with different stories and requirements" - "[REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT] valid mixed @story/@req/@supports usage in same block comment" Invalid cases cover: - "[REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE] @supports with no value is invalid" (missing story + reqs) - "[REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE] @supports with only story path and no requirement IDs is invalid" - "[REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION] @supports with invalid story path format" - "[REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION] @supports with invalid requirement ID format" and with one invalid among many. All these tests pass in the Jest run.,Deep validation that each @supports requirement exists in its specified story file (REQ-SUPPORTS-VALIDATE, REQ-SCOPED-IDS, REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT, REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT) is implemented in src/rules/helpers/valid-req-reference-helpers.ts: - parseImplementsLine(line) parses '@supports ' into storyPath and reqIds. - validateImplementsLine(...) resolves the story path via resolveStoryAndRequirements(), reads/ caches requirements per file (loadAndCacheRequirements), then iterates each reqId and calls checkRequirementExists(). - checkRequirementExists reports context.report({ messageId: 'reqMissing', data: { reqId, storyPath } }). - Requirement IDs are cached per resolvedStoryPath, allowing the same ID (e.g., REQ-SHARED-ID) to exist in multiple files without conflict, satisfying scoped IDs.,The deep validation rule src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts exposes message templates including story path (REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT): - reqMissing: "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'". - invalidPath: "Invalid story path '{{storyPath}}'". Tests in tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts (tagged with Story 010.0 and referencing Story 010.2 in names) exercise @supports behavior: - Valid: "[REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS] single supports line with multiple requirements in multi-story fixture (see 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT)" with `// @supports tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md REQ-SHARED-ID REQ-ONLY-A`. - Valid: "[REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS] multi-story supports with shared requirement IDs (see 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT)" with two @supports lines pointing to story_multi_a.md and story_multi_b.md, both using REQ-SHARED-ID. - Invalid: "[REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS] missing supports requirement in multi-story fixture (see 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT)" expecting messageId 'reqMissing' and data { reqId: 'REQ-NOT-IN-A', storyPath: 'tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md' }. - Invalid: "[REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS] disallow path traversal in supports story path (see 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT)" expecting messageId 'invalidPath' with the problematic storyPath. These tests confirm per-story validation, scoped IDs, and error messages that include the story path.,Backward compatibility and 'accept @supports as satisfying story/req rules' (REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-SUPPORTS, REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT, REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT) are implemented and tested: - For story presence, src/rules/helpers/require-story-io.ts commentContainsStory() returns true if comment.value includes '@story' or '@supports'; line scanning and fallback text detection similarly treat '@supports' as a valid marker, so require-story-annotation considers @supports coverage equivalent to @story. - For requirement presence, src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts commentContainsReq, linesBeforeHasReq, parentChainHasReq, fallbackTextBeforeHasReq, and hasReqInJsdocOrComments all treat both '@req' and '@supports' as satisfying requirement presence checks. - Tests in tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts (header includes @story for docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md and @req REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS) include a valid case named "[REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS] valid with only @implements annotation" whose code is `@supports docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED` and is accepted as valid story coverage. - Tests in tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts similarly include a valid case "[REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS] valid with only @implements annotation" where a function has only an @supports line; it is accepted as satisfying the requirement check via the shared detection helpers. - Additional tests in tests/utils/req-annotation-detection.test.ts explicitly assert that '@supports' in comments and JSDoc satisfies requirement detection (e.g. "treats @supports in comments as satisfying requirement" and "hasReqAnnotation returns true when jsdoc contains @supports...").,Mixed usage support (both styles in same file/comment) is directly tested in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts, which has a valid case named "[REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT] valid mixed @story/@req/@supports usage in same block comment" using: - @story docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md - @req REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT - @supports docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md REQ-IMPLEMENTS-PARSE REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT The validator helpers finalize @story and @req via finalizePendingAnnotation while treating @supports as immediate per-line checks, enabling clean coexistence of both annotation styles within the same comment and file.,Requirement scoping (REQ-SCOPED-IDS) is satisfied by implementation and tests: - src/rules/helpers/valid-req-reference-helpers.ts caches requirements by resolvedStoryPath in a Map<string, Set>. Each story file's requirements are extracted independently with regex /REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+/g, allowing the same requirement ID string to appear in multiple files without conflict. - tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts uses two fixture files tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md and story_multi_b.md, both containing REQ-SHARED-ID; the valid test "multi-story supports with shared requirement IDs" confirms that supports lines for each story file validate correctly. This demonstrates IDs are scoped per story file, not globally unique.,Error message context (REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT) for requirement validation failures is confirmed by tests: - valid-req-reference meta defines reqMissing: "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'". - tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts invalid cases assert both reqId and storyPath in error data for missing requirements, including for @supports lines (e.g. missing supports requirement in multi-story fixture). Thus, when validation fails, the checked story is clearly indicated.,Documentation and migration guidance (acceptance criterion 'Documentation') for @supports and multi-story behavior are present in user-facing docs: - user-docs/api-reference.md describes @supports alongside @story and @req, explains that require-story-annotation and require-req-annotation will accept @supports as alternative coverage, and notes that deep requirement checking for both @req and @supports is handled by valid-req-reference. It references the migration guide section on multi-story @supports. - user-docs/migration-guide.md has section "3.1 Multi-story @supports annotations" with explicit examples using @supports docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md REQ-... and guidance on how and when to migrate from @story/@req to @supports, and describes the optional prefer-supports-annotation migration rule. This matches the story’s requirement for clear examples and migration guidance.,Backward compatibility for existing @story + @req annotations is preserved and verified by the extensive pre-existing tests that still pass: - tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts contains many valid and invalid cases for plain @story and @req annotations unaffected by @supports support. - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts and tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts still assert that functions without any traceability annotations are reported (e.g. "[REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED][BACKCOMPAT] missing @story annotation on function with no @supports" remains invalid and auto-fix output is checked), confirming that enabling @supports did not weaken basic enforcement. - tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts and tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts maintain their original behaviors for @story/@req references, with @supports handling added alongside rather than replacing them.,Quality standards / ESLint rule best practices are followed for the new behavior: - All relevant rules (valid-annotation-format, valid-req-reference, require-story-annotation, require-req-annotation) define proper meta, docs, messages, and JSON schema; they use RuleTester-based unit tests. - Complex logic is factored into helpers (e.g., src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-format-validators.ts and src/rules/helpers/valid-req-reference-helpers.ts) in line with maintainable ESLint rule design. - Story and requirement IDs are annotated in JSDoc throughout the implementation, matching the project’s traceability standard.,Global test run including all tests for this story and its dependencies passes: - Command run: npm test -- --runInBand --verbose - Jest output shows all suites passing (45 passed, 45 total; 343 tests), including: - tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts (covers REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE, REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION, REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT for Story 010.2) - tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts (covers @supports deep validation and scoped IDs, referencing Story 010.2) - tests/utils/req-annotation-detection.test.ts (covers treating @supports as requirement coverage) - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts and tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts (cover REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-SUPPORTS for Story 010.2) - Exit code was 0, confirming all test coverage for this story currently passes.
traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria and technical requirements for Story 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT are fully implemented. The code supports @supports annotations, validates their format, performs deep per-story requirement existence checks, accepts @supports as satisfying both story and requirement presence rules, maintains backward compatibility with existing @story and @req annotations, supports mixed usage, and surfaces errors that clearly identify the story path. User-facing documentation (API reference and migration guide) describes multi-story @supports behavior and migration guidance. Comprehensive unit tests and integration tests tied explicitly to docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md all pass in the current test run. Therefore this story is PASSED.
